series_key: a dll for mql5 in 10 minutes
mechanism: Visual Studio 2017 walkthrough for building 64-bit MQL5 DLLs: export macros, .def files, DllMain pitfalls, string/struct packing, optional SMTP mailer. No market sensing construction.
why_new_for_mis: No sensing content after full read—pure language/interop tutorial.
quote: The article is intended for beginners who want to learn how to create and connect C++ libraries to the terminal.

mechanism: After a detected candlestick pattern on closed bars, GetCategory copies the next 3 bars and classifies whether High-Close0 (or Close0-Low) reaches a user Trend threshold in points within 1, 2, or 3 bars (buckets a_uptrend/b_uptrend/c_uptrend and dntrend mirrors). Yields empirical up/down hit rates and weighted efficiency coeffs k1/k2/k3 per pattern×TF.
data_needed: OHLC CopyRates over a calendar date range; pattern detectors; threshold in points; multi-TF button set M1–MN.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any MT5 symbols (EURUSD demo); selectable TFs M1,M2,…,H1,H4,D1,W1,MN; date-range sampling
why_new_for_mis: Turns classic candlestick hits into a scored post-event follow-through sensor (how far/how fast price moves after the pattern)—MIS can treat a/b/c reach buckets as change-quality features, not just pattern presence.
quote: the GetCategory() method checks the price behavior after pattern occurrence using historic data.

mechanism: GetCandleType labels local trend UPPER/DOWN/FLAT by comparing current Close to the average of the prior 5 closes on the working TF before assigning hammer/doji/etc. Pattern search (e.g. Hammer) further requires trend==DOWN.
data_needed: 5-bar close average + current OHLC on each TF.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit micro-regime bit (5-bar SMA vs close) gating pattern validity—MIS can reuse as a cheap local-trend feature fused with pattern detectors.
quote: if(aver<res.close) res.trend=UPPER; if(aver>res.close) res.trend=DOWN; if(aver==res.close) res.trend=FLAT;

mechanism: On a short Close window (≥32, demo 64) shifted by 1 bar, compute amplitude variation V(δ) of min-coverage rectangles at dyadic partitions, regress ln V vs ln δ to get fractal index μ (Hurst=1−μ). Classify: μ≈0.5 Brownian; μ<0.5 persistent/trend (“black”); μ>0.5 anti-persistent/flat (“pink”). Emits μ(t), 95% CI width, and KR2=1−R² stability.
data_needed: Close series; window power-of-two length; hourSampling; LogDeltaScales/LogAmplVariations LS fit.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Gazprom Close (demo 600 days, window 64); Alcoa Inc. overlapping 32-day windows; Lukoil 1999; day-scale sampling
why_new_for_mis: Local min-cover μ is a short-sample regime sensor that converges far faster than classical Hurst—MIS can stream μ/CI/KR2 as trend-vs-flat-vs-noise labels without needing 10k-point windows.
quote: Case μ <0.5 can be interpreted as a trend, and case μ >0.5 can be treated as a flat. μ ~ 0.5 is considered to be the Brownian motion.

mechanism: Author frames local μ(t) for detecting disorder—moments when statistical characteristics of the series change—because μ’s reliable scale is ~100× smaller than Hurst’s, so transitions among trend/flat/Brown states are timed as local change events.
data_needed: Rolling μ(t) series and thresholds around 0.5; optional CI/KR2 quality gate.
why_new_for_mis: Uses μ crossings of the 0.5 band (and color-coded state flips) as an explicit regime-change/disorder sensor—MIS change feature from fractal stability, not from MA crosses.
quote: Local fractal analysis can be interesting in trading for the following purposes: 1. Determining of disorder, i.e. of the moment when statistical characteristics of a time series change;

mechanism: Count N consecutive same-direction bars on a chosen TF (optimized M5–D1, N=3–7). Two opposite sensors: enter against the streak (expects correction after prolonged unidirectional move) or enter with the streak (expects trend continuation). First grid leg direction only; later legs follow adverse price steps.
data_needed: Bar open/close direction streaks; TF and N inputs; optional MA/prior-bar concurrence.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDCAD,NZDUSD Forex 2010–2019; SBUX,XOM,INTC,CMCSA,PG stocks 2013–2019; EA on M5; bar sensors on M15/H1/H4/D1/MN
why_new_for_mis: Simple streak-length event as either mean-reversion or breakout change gate—MIS can expose both polarities as discrete features with TF×N parameterization.
quote: if the price moved five bars in one direction, it is time to enter against the price assuming that a correction is on its way.

mechanism: DLL pulls https://www.mataf.net/.../volatility via libcurl into memory, Gumbo-parses table#volTable, finds tr#row_{PAIR}, reads TD column 2/3/4 as volatility by pips / USD / percent, returns double to MQL. Intended to be cached so EAs/indicators do not poll every tick.
data_needed: HTTP fetch of mataf volatility page; pair string; VOLTYPE∈{byPips,byCurr,byPerc}; optional file/memory cache TTL.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: FX pairs listed on mataf (e.g. EURUSD, AUDCHF); site-published volatility snapshot (not a chart TF)
why_new_for_mis: External cross-sectional FX volatility panel as a sensing feed (three units)—MIS can ingest third-party realized-vol tables alongside native bar vol without reinventing the scrape.
quote: Volatility data are contained in the table <table id="volTable" ... Each row consists of five columns. We do not need the first two columns, while the three others contain the required data.

mechanism: First grid position opens only on RSI(35) M5 extremes: RSI>80 → Short; RSI<30 → Long (fade). Grid step fixed in points; max chain length capped at 2 with hard stop at step-3 level. Diversification across FX pairs used to cut drawdown.
data_needed: iRSI period 35 on M5; thresholds 80/30; per-symbol grid step and TP.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDCAD,EURUSD,EURGBP,EURAUD,AUDNZD; EA TF M5; opt window 2018.10–2019.10; stock Long-only variant on VZ,MCD,JPM,KO,MSFT,NKE,ORCL,CSCO,EBAY
why_new_for_mis: RSI zone as a discrete overbought/oversold regime bit that arms a short-chain grid—MIS can reuse the 80/30 M5 RSI(35) state as a fade-regime feature independent of the martingale wrapper.
quote: If RSI value exceeds 80, open a Short trade. If RSI falls below 30, open a Long trade. It means that positions are opened against the current trend.

mechanism: Postscript stress-tests a multi-stock Long-only RSI averaging EA (≤4 steps) through the 2020 SPX crash; reports recovery-factor changes. No new sensing construction beyond prior RSI fade logic.
why_new_for_mis: After full read: portfolio stress narrative and lot-scaling tests, not a new MIS sensing idea.
quote: The main purpose of the article is to test the averaging and martingale-based EA in the market, for which it has not been initially intended.

mechanism: From the mouse bar’s High−Low, project vertical targets at fractional distances (default coefficient 0.825 ≈7/8 of 2×range, and 14/8) in the direction away from the cursor side; short horizontal stubs mark those prices. Encodes the heuristic that price often travels a similar distance after a large bar then stalls short of 100%.
data_needed: Bar High/Low under cursor; Vertical_Short_Level_Coefficient; Short_Level_Length in bars.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any chart (EURUSD H1 demos); TF-colored objects; works across M1–MN via U/D TF switch
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes measured-move / fractional-extension levels as explicit geometric projection sensors—MIS can auto-emit 7/8 and 14/8 targets from impulse bars without manual drawing.
quote: most often the following rule can be used for trading: the price always tends to move by the same distance that it has already passed.

mechanism: Derives cycle math for grids/martingale and proves that lot/sequence manipulation without knowing approximate movement direction (or auxiliary market parameters) yields expected payoff →0; unfinished cycles wipe gains. Builds demo EAs that confirm eventual ruin. Conceptual warning, not a sensor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic Forex tester runs for Easy_Grid / Uncle_Martin demos
why_new_for_mis: After full read: mathematical critique of volume games without a forecast—no implementable sensing construction.
quote: all strategies involving variation and manipulating deal volumes, as well as order opening/closing systems of any complexity are doomed to fail without knowing the approximate movement direction

mechanism: Over CandlesE bars, split bullish vs bearish bars and accumulate PowerUp/PowerDown. Four modes: (1) (body/range)×tick volume; (2) body_points×volume; (3)/(4) same with linear recency weight (CandlesE−i)/CandlesE. Emit |BarsUp−BarsDown| as Signal strength and PercentPowerUp/Down; trade when Signal≥threshold and power %≥PercentE inside a server-time corridor.
data_needed: OHLCV Copy* arrays; MODE_1..4; CandlesE; Signal; PercentE; TradeHour/Minute session window.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M5 primary tests; 2010–2020 segments; designed multi-currency; bar-close only
why_new_for_mis: Volume×body/range directional power with optional temporal decay is a concrete microstructure imbalance sensor—MIS can stream PercentPower and Signal as participation-weighted regime/pressure features.

mechanism: Convert last-tick server time to minute-of-day and allow new entries only inside [TradeHour:TradeMinute, TradeHourEnd:TradeMinuteEnd] (supports wrap-over-midnight). Author treats the corridor as selecting hours where bar-volume signals matter most.
data_needed: MqlDateTime from LastTick.time; four HH:MM inputs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same VolumesAndIntervals EA; EURUSD M5; corridor tuned per experiment
why_new_for_mis: Explicit intraday regime mask for when volume-power features are trusted—MIS can attach TOD corridors as enable bits on other sensors.
quote: Strange as it may seem, this value defines a lot.

mechanism: Bar-based simulator plants grids of stop/limit/market virtual orders per bar (equal or distance-attenuated weights), ages them into market or aborted, decays VolumeAlpha by price progress toward TP/SL and by bar expiration, then reports BuyPercent/SellPercent of remaining market volume. Trade when one side’s % is in [MinPercentE,MaxPercentE] and RelativeVolume in band—fade the dominant simulated side.
data_needed: OHLC history BarsE; HalfCorridor; OrdersToOneBar; Expiration* ; Profit/Loss point corridors; VolumeAlphaStop/Limit/Market weights.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; best on M5; MT4 2010–2020 then MT5 real-tick forward 2020; multi-pair potential noted
why_new_for_mis: Proxy order-book imbalance from OHLC-only simulation (Buy% vs Sell%)—MIS liquidity/pressure sensor when true book data is absent.

mechanism: RelativeVolume = |SummVolumeBuy−SummVolumeSell| / StartVolume measures how “full” the simulated book’s uncovered side is versus the initial planted volume mass. Used with Min/MaxRelativeVolumeE as a second gate so signals fire only at intermediate imbalance intensity (not empty, not saturated).
data_needed: StartVolume from initial grid weights; current SummVolumeBuy/Sell after Update*.
why_new_for_mis: Scalar market-filling intensity complements side%—MIS can treat RelativeVolume as a liquidity-stress / crowding feature on top of directional imbalance.

mechanism: Product/community guide to MQL5 channels vs group chats, broker support threads, and mobile messenger. No market sensing.
why_new_for_mis: No sensing content after full read—platform UX documentation.
quote: Use chats for private messages, create group chats or broadcast trading ideas to large audiences through channels.
